items.title: FedEx: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: FedEx raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance following strong Q3 2026 earnings. The company is executing Network 2.0 optimization targeting $2 billion in cumulative savings by 2027, accelerating share buybacks as free cash flow expands, and strategically shifting toward higher-margin B2B and international cargo while shedding low-margin domestic shipments. International export volume grew 8% year-over-year, supporting margin expansion.

items.title: FedEx Q3 Earnings Top Estimates on Higher Yields, 2026 Outlook Raised
items.summary: FedEx exceeded Q3 earnings and revenue expectations with $3.74 EPS and $22.86B in revenues, driven by higher package yields, international growth, and Network 2.0 cost savings. The company raised its 2026 EPS guidance to $18.00-$18.60 and expects ~12% revenue growth. Other transportation peers showed mixed results, with Delta and United missing estimates while J.B. Hunt beat expectations.

items.title: FedEx Gears Up for Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: FedEx is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 28 with consensus EPS estimates cut 30.6% to $3.24. The company faces headwinds from higher wages, transportation costs, a $200M pilot contract expense, and stranded costs from the FedEx Freight spin-off. However, Network 2.0 savings and healthy pricing may provide some offset.

items.title: United Parcel Service vs. FedEx: What Their Revenue Trends Tell Investors
items.summary: FedEx demonstrates stronger revenue momentum with consistent year-over-year growth and steady quarterly expansion, while UPS experiences volatile quarterly performance due to its strategic decision to shed low-margin Amazon business and prioritize profit margins over revenue growth. FedEx's recent freight spinoff and expected 11% fiscal year growth contrast with UPS's intentional volume reduction driven by higher unionized labor costs.
